3. Results

3.1 Reproduction of the reference epidemic trajectory

The parameters determined using the pseudo HER-SYS data are shown in Table 1 (which also includes parameters for other cases described later). The simulation results obtained with this parameter set are presented in Figure 2. It can be seen that the pseudo HER-SYS data used (also shown in the figure) are reproduced with a high accuracy. The results are highly similar to Figure 1 in the Kayano–Nishiura paper, confirming that the optimization using the pseudo HER-SYS data in this study is reliable. To complement this visual comparison, approximate normalized fit metrics were also estimated from graphically extracted trajectories of the fitted curve. For the Original case, the resulting values were RMSE/peak ≈ 0.030 and MAE/peak ≈ 0.018. Although these values are only approximate and are not intended as formal model selection criteria, they are consistent with close agreement between the fitted trajectory and the reference data.

3.2 Effect of suppressing the vaccination-related input

Figure 3 shows the fitted trajectory obtained after the vaccination-related input was suppressed and the remaining adjustable parameters were re-estimated against the reference epidemic trajectory. The optimized parameters are listed in Table 1. Despite suppression of the vaccination-related contribution, the refitted model retained close agreement with the reference trajectory. Approximate normalized fit metrics estimated from graphically extracted trajectories were RMSE/peak ≈ 0.039 and MAE/peak ≈ 0.025, compared with RMSE/peak ≈ 0.030 and MAE/peak ≈ 0.018 for the Original case.

Figure 3:

Reproduction of the reference epidemic trajectory after suppression of the vaccination-related input (solid line).

Thus, suppressing the vaccination-related input produced only a limited deterioration in trajectory-level fit after re-estimation of the remaining parameters. This result shows that close agreement with the reference epidemic trajectory can be maintained in this model even when the vaccination-related contribution is not active. It does not establish formal non-identifiability of that contribution, but demonstrates that goodness-of-fit alone does not require its inclusion to obtain a close reproduction of the reference trajectory.

3.3 Fitting to synthetic target trajectories

Figure 4 shows the results of fitting the Kayano–Nishiura model to the two synthetic target series. The optimized parameters are listed in Table 1. In both the FDH (Figure 4(a)) and FSH (Figure 4(b)) cases, parameter re-estimation allowed the model to reproduce the main temporal features of the target trajectories despite their qualitatively different shapes.
